inflation_management: Niue is self-governing in free association with New Zealand, uses the New Zealand dollar, and has no monetary policy or IMF data. With around 1,700 residents, there is barely a price level to manage - nearly everything is imported, and inflation is whatever New Zealand's is plus freight. Aid, remittances and .nu domain revenues fund consumption; tourism is small but growing.
debt_management: Niue carries no meaningful sovereign debt; its 'fiscal policy' is allocating New Zealand aid, domain-name income and modest tourism receipts. The long-running dispute over control and revenue of the .nu internet domain is the closest thing to a sovereign-wealth question. Economic viability rests entirely on external support, which Wellington provides steadily.

key_events.event: COVID-19 border closure cut the nascent tourism sector; reopening was slow and cautious.
Ongoing dispute with Sweden's IIS foundation over control of the lucrative .nu domain.

outlook_next_decade: Niue will remain a subsidized microstate; the realistic goal is not growth but viability - keeping population from declining further through tourism, remote-work visas and domain income. New Zealand's backing is assured. Climate resilience for water and the single hospital-scale infrastructure is the practical agenda. Expect quiet stability, not economic takeoff.
caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
